subject: Trouble initializing with a hierarchical weibull model

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Trouble initializing with a hierarchical weibull model
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm feel like I must be missing something basic here, but I can't seem to get a pretty simple model to initialize. The model is here:

https://gist.github.com/mike-lawrence/6043738

The model compiles fine, but upon initialization I get the error:

"Error in function stan::prob::lognormal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable[0]  is nan:0, but must not be nan!Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density."

Many times, then finally:

"Initialization failed after 100 attempts.  Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model."

Which is curious, because when I convert the stan code to a single sampling attempt in R (see last block in the code linked above), the sample comes out perfectly fine. 

So, what head-smackingly simple thing have I missed this time? :O)

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trouble initializing with a hierarchical weibull model
parts:
The problem is here:

model {
vector[N] scale;
vector[N] shape;
vector[L] thisScale;
vector[L] thisShape;
scalePopMean ~ uniform(4,6);
shapePopMean ~ uniform(0,2);
scalePopSD ~ uniform(0,1);
shapePopSD ~ uniform(0,1);
scale ~ lognormal(scalePopMean,scalePopSD);
shape ~ lognormal(shapePopMean,shapePopSD);
for(i in 1:L){
thisScale[i] <- scale[unit[i]];
thisShape[i] <- shape[unit[i]];
}
y ~ weibull(thisShape,thisScale);
}

When you call scale ~ lognormal(...) the variable scale is
not set (we default initialize to NaN just to trap errors
like this --- we haven't figured out how to have a good warning
message for using undefined vars yet).

The sampling statements in Stan do not do sampling
per se, they just evaluate the log probability. If they're unknown,
then you need to make them parameters rather than local variables
in the model.

I'd also add a lower bound to this to check the data's kosher:

vector[L] y;

should have vector<lower=0>[L] to make sure the data's in range.

- Bob

Thanks, and apologies: I see now that I asked a similar question last spring where I similarly failed to put a parameter in the parameter block. Hopefully that'll stick now!

However, moving both "vector[N] scale" and "vector[N] shape" to the parameter block continues to yield the initialization failure, this time with error messages indicating that something relating to my calls to lognormal() yields something negative when it should be positive, as in:

Error in function stan::prob::lognormal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable[0]  is -1.6254974062520904:0, but must be >= 0!Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.

Any suggestions on what I might still be doing improperly?

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University
